blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Gupta Empire was founded by Sri Gupta, but Chandragupta I established it as a major empire and started the Gupta Era in 319–320 CE.
Samudragupta expanded the empire across northern and southern India and was designated the 'Napoleon of India' by V.A. Smith.
Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) patronized the Nine Gems (Navaratnas), including the court poet Kalidasa and astronomer Varahamihira.
Nalanda Mahavihara was established during the reign of Kumaragupta I as an international seat of learning.
Skandagupta successfully repelled the first waves of Huna invasions, though later invasions eventually weakened the empire.

blocks.content: The Gupta period is widely regarded as the Golden Age of Ancient India due to magnificent achievements in art, architecture, literature, astronomy, and mathematics.

rows: Established political supremacy and started the Gupta Era (319–320 CE)
Military conquests recorded in Harisena's Prayag Prashasti
Patronized the Navaratnas; Faxian visited during his reign
Founded the famous Nalanda University; performed Ashvamedha Yajna
Repulsed the formidable Huna invasions to safeguard the realm

items: Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) was written in Sanskrit by court poet Harisena using the Champu kavya style.
Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Faxian (Fa-Hien) visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II.
Gupta monarchs issued the largest number of gold coins (Dinara) in ancient India.
Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda University, while Skandagupta is celebrated for defeating the Hunas.
